text_blocks.snippet: A hereditary blood clot disorder, also known as inherited thrombophilia, is a condition where a person has a genetic predisposition to developing blood clots due to inherited mutations in genes that affect blood clotting. These mutations can lead to an increased tendency for blood to clot, potentially causing deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or pulmonary embolism (PE).
snippet_highlighted_words: a condition where a person has a genetic predisposition to developing blood clots due to inherited mutations in genes that affect blood clotting

text_blocks.snippet: Key aspects of hereditary blood clot disorders:

list.title: Genetic Basis:
list.snippet: These disorders are caused by inherited gene mutations that disrupt the normal blood clotting process.

list.title: Increased Risk:
list.snippet: Individuals with inherited thrombophilia have a higher risk of developing blood clots, particularly in veins.
